dedupe_keys.name: crowd behaviours in emergency evacuation matlab model of exit congestion based on evolutionary game theory

description: This model studies how behaviours spread through a crowd during an emergency evacuation, using evolutionary game theory. It was written in MATLAB by Azhar Mohd Ibrahim and published in the CoMSES library in 2018. People move in continuous space towards exits under uncertainty; when two of them try to move into the same place, a conflict is resolved as a game, and each person's response to its nearest neighbours changes the strategies that spread through the crowd. The aim is to show how the mix of behaviours affects congestion at exits and so to support crowd control planning for large gatherings. Version 1.0.0 is available as a free download from CoMSES under the Apache-2.0 licence. Caveats: MATLAB is needed to run it, the geometry is generic, and the page reports no validation against real evacuations. Coverage is general. Simulation uses: exploring how crowd behaviour changes evacuation times for venues and public buildings, alongside engineering egress tools. Related records: the Jülich pedestrian dynamics data archive (data-juelich-pedestrian-dynamics-data-archive) provides experimental crowd data for calibration.
inputs: Room or space geometry with exits
name: Crowd behaviours in emergency evacuation: MATLAB model of exit congestion based on evolutionary game theory
outputs: Evacuation progress and the evolution of cooperative and competitive behaviours at congested exits
